newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila Central Bank seen selling dlrs at 26.375.
newsitem.headline: Manila Central Bank seen selling dlrs at 26.375.

text.p: The Philippine Central Bank sold dollars at a rate of 26.375 pesos in midsession on Wednesday, up from its previous selling rate of 26.37, traders said.
They estimate the Central Bank may have already sold more than $100 million at the rates of 26.37 and 26.375.
Banks are currently nervous over possible outflows from foreign funds divesting their stock market investments in Manila.
The Central Bank moved its selling rate to discourage banks from buying dollars from the bank. But banks still decided to get dollars from the Central Bank, a trader said.
"The market panicked...(the more the Bank raised its rate) the more the market lifted from him," another dealer said.
The peso had so far traded from 26.37/26.375 with volume heavy at $228 million.
